title: Native Video CD Contents control stalls
symptom: Selecting Contents in the native Video CD menu makes the in-disc controls stop responding in two tested Video CDs, while MPEG video continues playing.
expected: The native Contents action opens or navigates the disc's content selection and the Video CD controls remain responsive.
revalidation_reason: Manually reproduced in two current-build Video CD runs. Continued MPEG playback shows that the decoder and presentation clocks continue, but no device boundary has yet been isolated.

input_events: open the native Video CD controls

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The native Video CD application may be waiting for a CDIC/CDFM or PSD-navigation completion that E-Di does not deliver, or input/control state may fail to transition after the Contents action. MPEG playback can continue independently while the guest control path waits.
supporting_evidence: The in-disc controls stop responding immediately after Contents is selected in two tested Video CDs.
MPEG video continues playing, so this is not a total machine or decoder freeze.
contradicting_evidence: No bounded guest-PC, input-packet, CDIC-command, PSD, or completion-event trace has been captured around the click.
The exact second disc fingerprint and whether both discs use the same PSD layout are not yet recorded.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Record two deterministic runs around the Contents selection, one without the click and one with it. Compare SLAVE input delivery, guest PC/IRQ state, CDIC commands and completions, VCD PSD reads, and VMPEG counters to identify the first control-path divergence.
citations: Video CD on CD-i Release 4.1, control behavior and PSD startup
White Book Video CD playback control

manual_verification.notes: The native Contents control became unresponsive in two tested Video CDs while the feature video continued to decode and play.
